<strong>Convierte con método, no de memo: Convert with method, not from memory. To change base, divide and note the remainders; for two's complement, invert and add one. Rushing in binary costs more marks than anywhere else in the course.
<strong>Dibuja el árbol antes de evaluar: Draw the tree before evaluating. With precedence properly set, the Polish notation and the assembly come out by themselves; without a tree, they come out “nearly” right, which is wrong.
<strong>Lo que falles, ábrelo en el banc: Whatever you get wrong, open it on the bench or on the machine. Each question links to its topic, and there the circuit, the CPU or the language can really be run: it is the most instructive kind of marking.
<strong>Sigue los programas con una tabl: Follow the programs with a table. One column per register and another for the program counter, one row per instruction executed. It is what the machine does, and what stops you getting lost in a jump.
A la tercera vuelta ya no se recuerda qu: By the third turn you no longer remember what each register held. The table is not optional: it is the machine on paper.
Cada tramo aporta un número fijo de preg: Each section contributes a fixed number of questions, chosen at random among its topics without repeating a topic while possible, and avoiding the most basic exercises. With 18 topics and 10 questions, a single exam does not touch them all: that is why the link at the end reproduces the same exam, and “another exam” brings out a different one.
Casi ningún ejercicio pide un bucle infi: Hardly any exercise asks for an infinite loop. Before giving up, look at which register decides the jump and how it changes on each turn.
Cómo sacarle partido: How to get the most out of it
Dieciocho temas, dos tramos que se cierr: Eighteen topics, two stretches that close on each other: the compiler of [[len-compilar]] generates the assembly for the CPU of [[maq-cpu]]. This topic teaches nothing new: it asks. A procedural exam with exercises from the whole block, with a clock and no hints, to find out whether what lies between the bit and the language has really sunk in.
Ejecutarlo mentalmente sin apuntar nada: Run it in your head without writing anything down
El enlace de un examen corregido reprodu: The link to a marked exam reproduces the same questions with the same numbers. A teacher can do one, copy the link and pass it to the class: everyone will sit the same exam and will be able to compare results and procedures.
Elige los tramos que entran. Las pregunt: Choose the sections to include. The questions are drawn at random from the exercises of each topic in the block, avoiding the most basic ones and without repeating a topic while possible. There are no hints: the marking and the step-by-step solution come on submitting.
En una pregunta de ensamblador el progra: In an assembly question the program jumps backwards and you cannot see when it ends. What do you do?
Los primeros exámenes de «programación»: The first “programming” exams in history were taken without a computer: at the University of Cambridge, in the late nineteen-forties, the EDSAC students handed in the program on paper and another student played the machine, following the instructions one by one with a pencil. Following a program with a register table, as in this exam, is exactly that exercise, and it is still the surest way to understand what a machine does.
Pasar de binario a hexadecimal y a compl: Converting from binary to hexadecimal and to two's complement; writing the truth table of a gate or of a circuit; the carry of an adder; simplifying a normal form.
Qué guarda un biestable y por qué es un: What a flip-flop stores and why it is a loop; the fetch-decode-execute cycle; following an assembly program step by step, with jumps and a stack.
Resolver un nombre en su ámbito; contar: Resolving a name in its scope; counting the frames a recursion creates; translating an expression into assembly; folding constants and removing dead code; the program that prints itself.
Seguir la tabla de registros hasta que l: Follow the register table until the jump's condition stops holding
Suponer que es un bucle infinito y pasar: Assume it is an infinite loop and move to another question
Trocear una línea en tokens; decidir si: Splitting a line into tokens; deciding whether a grammar generates a sentence; drawing the tree of an expression respecting precedence; evaluating in reverse Polish notation.
Un bucle termina cuando su condición cam: A loop ends when its condition changes, and that shows in the table: the register being compared keeps changing on each turn. Three or four turns are enough to see the pattern.
Un examen de bloque es un simulacro hech: A block exam is a mock done at home: with a clock, no notes and no hints. The questions come from the exercises of the block's 18 topics, spread across sections, and each time you start one the numbers are different and so are the topics: doing it several times covers the whole block. On submitting, everything is marked, the step-by-step solution to each question opens and the mark comes out by section, with links to what is worth revising. The “tailored to what you have done” option puts first what you have not yet solved: it is the way to check that no topic is left untouched.
